newsitem.title: USA: Conrail head to get $22 million severance - consultant. [CORRECTED 08:03 GMT 15/3]
newsitem.headline: Conrail head to get $22 million severance - consultant. [CORRECTED 08:03 GMT 15/3]

text.p: Conrail Inc. Chairman David LeVan is to receive $22 million as part of a $1.15 billion severance package for executives and other non-union employees of the soon-to-be divided railroad, an analysis of the terms shows.

The estimate was prepared by an outside actuarial expert for CSX Corp., which is to buy Conrail for $10.3 billion cash, and was based on terms contained in the two companies' merger pact. A copy of the analysis was obtained by Reuters Friday.
Conrail spokesman Bob Libkind declined to comment on the analysis. "We don't comment on anything we didn't produce," he said, adding details of severance packages are not complete.
A CSX spokesman who declined to be identified said in reference to the terms, "CSX believes that Conrail employees are worth it and deserve it."
The cost of the severance packages to CSX will be $878 million, plus $274 million in already allocated shares Conrail workers are to receive under an employee stock program.

Conrail's roughly 19,000 unionized employees are covered separately under a federal law that would make them eligible for continued pay and benefits for up to six years (corrects terms of federal law) if they lose their jobs as a result of a merger, Libkind said.
Conrail and CSX agreed on the revised merger last week. CSX is to negotiate a division of Conrail with Norfolk Southern Corp., which had pursued a separate hostile takeover of Conrail.

The 79 Conrail executives of vice-president level and above who are to leave will receive packages worth an average of $1.54 million, including $1.26 million in severance bonuses and incentives to stay through a transition, according to the analysis.

In addition, an estimated 1,659 Conrail salaried employees below vice president level who will be remaining under the merger will receive incentives to stay with the company and stock worth an average of about $306,000 apiece.
The stock portion, averaging $278,058 per employee, includes previously allocated shares under a stock ownership program and accelerated allocations of shares not previously designated.
The estimated 1,187 junior-grade salaried employees who will be leaving the company are to receive bonuses, severance pay and stock worth an average of $420,00 apiece.
